text: Number two is the War of the Bucket in thirteen twenty-five.
Italian soldiers stole a plain wooden bucket right from a town well.
Its owner treated the theft as an insult and declared war.
Knights died charging hills while the bucket just sat inside the tower.
Around two thousand people died over one simple wooden bucket of oak.
The precious bucket still exists, and you can visit it today.
Stupidity rating, a perfect ten wooden buckets out of ten.
Number three on our list is the Pastry War of eighteen thirty-eight.
A French chef's beloved bakery got wrecked during a Mexico City riot.
France demanded six hundred thousand pesos for the completely ruined pastries.
